post.description: End an ongoing call and set ``ended_at``/``duration``. No body. An inbound call that was never answered ends as ``missed`` (which queues the ``call_missed`` notification), unless another agent's leg of the same queue attempt was already answered, in which case it ends as ``cancelled`` (answered elsewhere: counted neither as answered nor as missed). A ``missed`` leg is also re-labelled ``cancelled`` later when the queue's next agent answers (sequential strategies such as rrmemory), and then nobody is notified. Ending a leg that is already ``cancelled`` is a 200 no-op (the softphone may end it after the server relabelled it); 400 when the call is over for any other reason. Only the call's handling agent (``handled_by``), staff/superusers and PBX admins may end it (403 otherwise).

Browse active products with filtering options.

        **Dynamic Attribute Filters:**
        Filter by any product attribute using the pattern `attr_{attribute_key}`.
        The available attribute filters are dynamically generated based on your attribute definitions.

        Examples:
        - `?attr_color=red` - Single value
        - `?attr_color=red,blue,green` - Multiple values (OR logic)
        - `?attr_size=large&attr_color=red` - Multiple attributes (AND logic)
        - `?attr_width=10-20` - Number ranges
        - `?attr_waterproof=true` - Boolean values

        **Ordering Options:**
        - `?ordering=price` - Sort by price ascending
        - `?ordering=-price` - Sort by price descending
        - `?ordering=created_at` - Sort by creation date ascending (oldest first)
        - `?ordering=-created_at` - Sort by creation date descending (newest first)
        - `?ordering=name` - Sort by name ascending
        - `?ordering=-name` - Sort by name descending

        **Pagination:**
        - `?page=2` - Get specific page
        - `?page_size=50` - Items per page (default: 20, max: 100)

        **Other Filters:**
        - Basic: `?is_featured=true`
        - On Sale: `?on_sale=true`
        - Search: `?search=laptop`
        - Price: `?min_price=100&max_price=500`
        - Language: `?language=ka`

post.description: Enable or disable the IP whitelist and/or the superadmin bypass. Staff or superuser only. Both fields are optional; omitted ones keep their value. Enabling needs at least one active entry (400 `code: no_active_entries`). A change that would leave the whitelist on without letting the caller's current IP through is refused with 400 `code: would_lock_out` (the bypass only counts for superusers). Only a superuser can change `superadmin_bypass` (403 `code: bypass_superuser_only`). A caller who is not a superuser cannot enable the whitelist (bypass off) so that no active superuser's last sign-in IP is covered (400 `code: would_lock_out_superusers`). Values that are not booleans (form strings true/false/1/0 are accepted) return 400 `code: invalid`. The caller IP is the first X-Forwarded-For entry.

post.description: Bulk action on messages selected by `message_ids` (pks) or by `thread_id`; one of the two is required. Actions: mark_read / mark_unread (also toggles is_read_by_staff), star / unstar, label / unlabel (needs `label`), move (needs `folder`), delete, restore. Optional `connection_id` limits a `thread_id` action to one mailbox. For delete with `thread_id`, optional `folder` is the folder being viewed: only the thread's messages there are deleted (purged when it is Trash, else moved to Trash). Outlook semantics: delete on a message outside Trash moves it to the mailbox's Trash (folder='Trash', previous_folder=<old folder>); delete on a message already in Trash removes it permanently (is_deleted=true). restore moves a Trash message back to previous_folder (default INBOX); rows soft-deleted by the old DB-only delete are simply un-deleted. delete / restore / move need send permission (403 otherwise). The DB changes immediately; the server write (MOVE, \Seen, \Flagged, UID EXPUNGE) runs in a background task and never fails the request. Messages on connections the user cannot access are ignored; 404 when nothing matched. Mailbox visibility (EmailConnectionUserAssignment) is decided per connection, with the same rule as /email/status/, /unread-count/ and the unified conversations: a connection with no user assignments is a shared inbox visible to everyone; a connection with assignments is visible only to its assignees. Admins, superusers, staff and users with the manage_social_connections permission see every connection. A user can therefore only ever receive messages of connections listed in /email/status/ `connections`.

Mailbox visibility (EmailConnectionUserAssignment) is decided per connection, with the same rule as /email/status/, /unread-count/ and the unified conversations: a connection with no user assignments is a shared inbox visible to everyone; a connection with assignments is visible only to its assignees. post.description: Re-tests IMAP (and SMTP when a new password is given) and, on success, sets is_active=True and clears auto_disabled_at. Admin / manage_social_connections only.

Send a new message, a reply (`reply_to_message_id` = pk of the message being answered, on any mailbox the user can access, else 400; the original is marked answered) or a forward (`forward_message_id` = pk of the forwarded message: its stored attachments are re-attached). Accepts `application/json`, or `multipart/form-data` when attaching files: repeat the `attachments` form key once per file and repeat list keys (`to_emails`, `cc_emails`, `bcc_emails`) once per address. At least one of `body_text` / `body_html` is required. The effective signature (see `effective_signature` on /email/status/) is appended server-side unless `signature_included` is true. `draft_id` deletes that draft after a successful send. The sent copy is stored in folder 'Sent' (exactly as delivered) and returned as `data`; it is also APPENDed to the server's Sent folder in the background. `refused_recipients` lists addresses the server refused when others were accepted; `warnings` holds non-fatal problems. `connection_id` must be an active mailbox the user can access (404 otherwise); when omitted the original's mailbox (replies) or the first accessible active mailbox is used. Mailbox visibility (EmailConnectionUserAssignment) is decided per connection, with the same rule as /email/status/, /unread-count/ and the unified conversations: a connection with no user assignments is a shared inbox visible to everyone; a connection with assignments is visible only to its assignees. Admins, superusers, staff and users with the manage_social_connections permission see every connection. A user can therefore only ever receive messages of connections listed in /email/status/ `connections`.

post.description: Apply one action to several users. Needs `manage_users` or staff. `change_role` needs `role`; `add_to_group` / `remove_from_group` need `group_id`; `reset_password` emails each user a fresh temporary password and signs them out. You are never deactivated, deleted or reset by your own bulk action, and non-superusers cannot touch superusers; such ids come back in `skipped_user_ids`. Granting the admin role (or changing an admin's role) needs a superuser: granting returns 403, admins in a role change are skipped. Non-staff callers also get 403 for a `role` above their own, and a role change skips users with privileges you lack; nobody but a superuser can raise their own role (you are skipped). `activate` skips the same users as `deactivate`. `reset_password` also skips users with privileges you lack (a higher role, a permission you do not have, staff). `deactivate` / `delete` skip staff and admin-role users unless you are staff, and users with privileges you lack. `add_to_group` / `remove_from_group` additionally need `manage_groups` or staff. Deactivating signs the users out of every session.

EmailMessageLite.description:
Lightweight row for ``GET /api/social/email-messages/?lite=1``
(and ``GET /api/social/email-messages/lite/``). OpenAPI component
``EmailMessageLite``.

Drops ``body_text`` / ``body_html`` / ``attachments`` (the bulk of every
row) and adds ``snippet`` (first 160 characters of ``body_text`` with
whitespace collapsed) and ``attachments_count`` so a phone can render an
inbox list from a ~10x smaller payload. Everything else — sender,
recipients, subject, dates, flags, labels, connection — is identical to
:class:`EmailMessageSerializer`.

SoftphoneSipConfiguration.description:
``SipConfigurationDetail`` as the softphone endpoints return it
(``webrtc_config``, ``my_config.sip_configuration``), plus:

* ``sip_enabled``: true when ``username``/``password`` hold credentials
  the caller may register with, false when they are blank (no extension
  of their own), so the client can skip SIP registration.
* ``wss_url``: the SIP WebSocket URL to connect to (the tenant's active
  PbxServer's ``wss_url`` when set, else built from ``sip_server`` /
  ``sip_port`` / ``websocket_path``; ``ws://`` only for localhost /
  ``*.lvh.me``).
* ``ice_servers``: ``[{urls, username?, credential?}]`` for the peer
  connection. When the configuration has a coturn ``turn_auth_secret``
  the TURN entry carries ephemeral credentials (12 h) and
  ``turn_password`` is ``''``; otherwise the static ``turn_username`` /
  ``turn_password`` pair is used in both places.

UserDirectory.description:
Slim, read-only user row for the people directory (``?lite=1``).

Everything here comes from the user row itself, ``select_related``
``department``/``manager`` and a ``prefetch_related('tenant_groups')``;
there is no per-row permission or feature computation, so a page of
rows costs a constant number of queries.
